person: Grace Lindqvist is a 59-year-old retired librarian, court-appointed personal representative of her mother Ingrid's estate; her mother died earlier this month, three states away, and her father, a veteran, died two years ago. Her mother's mail comes forwarded in batches and Grace reads it slowly, on a laptop she is not at ease with. She answers to the probate court and to her two siblings, Karl and Birgit, who want it finished and fair. She is grieving and tired, and wants to be told one step at a time what is needed from her and what Athena can find by herself.
stated_up_front: Hello, my mother Ingrid passed away this month and I am the one the court named to see to her estate. Her mail is coming to me in batches and I don't know where to start, so could you please help me one step at a time? I'm sorry if I lose the thread, there is so much this week.

facts.about: Mother's name and date of death
facts.truth: Ingrid Marie Lindqvist, died October 6, 2026, aged 86, a widow.
Appointed personal representative by the county probate court on October 14, 2026; she holds the letters of appointment.
Brother Karl and sister Birgit; all three are equal heirs under the will.
The funeral home quoted a package of $9,450, but its own printed price list adds up to about $8,700; she has not paid it yet.
Her father Nils, a Navy veteran, died in 2024; the family paid his burial of about $7,200 themselves, and nobody ever asked the VA about reimbursement.
Ingrid held a traditional IRA at Fidelity of roughly $64,000, with the three children as beneficiaries; Grace has not touched it.
The estate account at Lakeshore Community Credit Union was opened October 17 with a $11,300 deposit from her mother's checking; nothing has been paid from it.
Her mother's Medigap plan drafted a $187 premium on October 15, after her death; Grace noticed it on the bank statement.
Her mother was in the hospital for 4 days in September; Grace has a $3,140 bill from the hospital and doesn't know whether insurance paid it.
A collector wrote for a $2,860 credit card balance and suggested Grace could put it on her own card to settle; she has not replied.
Mail arrives forwarded about once a week; her mother's old tax returns and the will are scanned into a Drive folder named 'Mom'.

unknowns: Whether her mother had a life insurance policy or an old retiree group policy through her late husband's or her own job
Whether the hospital bill was already paid by the Medigap plan
The deadline for creditors to file claims, and the date by which a disclaimer must be made
Whether Social Security will pay the $255 death payment or whether the Treasury pulled anything back
Whether the unclaimed-property record under her mother's name is really her mother's
